analysis.title: UBS Daily Consumer/Lux 28 Oct: Heineken (+ve), Remy (+ve), Unilever (+ve), Danone (/)
key_insights: Heineken Q3 organic volume +3.9% vs company-compiled consensus +1.8% (UBSe +2.1%), a beat across all regions led by Asia Pacific (+15.6% vs +5.6% cons). Revenue per hectolitre +0.7%, or +1.8% excluding negative country mix from Vietnam and India (-110bps). FY26 guidance unchanged, positive translational FX adds upside. UBS sees shares up mid-single digits.

Heineken read-across: Americas (+1.8% vs +1.6% cons, Mexico and Brazil both growing) is positive for ABI. Asia Pacific is positive for ABI and Carlsberg. India is positive for Carlsberg. Europe +0.6% vs +0.3% cons is a beat and the weakness is likely already in Carlsberg numbers.

Remy Cointreau Q2 FY27 organic sales +4.2% vs cons +3.6% (UBSe +6.5%), driven by Remy Martin +12.4% vs cons +9.1%, with China shipments pulled forward ahead of the Mid-Autumn Festival. Liqueurs & Spirits -7.4% vs cons -3.5% on US destocking after distribution changes. Guidance broadly unchanged, but the currency assumption moved to a +€15m sales benefit from -€15m, which offers potential upgrades.
Remy tariff impact on current operating profit is now c.€5m vs c.€20m before. The c.€15m benefit will be fully reinvested in growth, so the organic margin objective is unchanged.

Unilever Q3 underlying sales growth +5.2% vs company cons +4.8%, volume +2.9% vs +2.5% cons. Asia Pacific Africa +10.1% vs +6.7% cons (India +15%, Indonesia +7%) was the major upside surprise. Home Care +9.1% vs +6.7% cons. North America -0.7% vs +1.4% cons and Europe -1.7% vs +0.5% cons were soft.

Unilever raised FY26 volume guidance to at least +3% (from around +3%) and H2 underlying sales growth to around +5% (from +4-5%), led by pricing. FY26 USG range of 4-6% and the margin outlook are unchanged. UBS carries a Sell rating on the name.

Danone Q3 like-for-like growth +4.0% vs cons +3.7%, but volume/mix +0.4% missed cons +0.9% while pricing +3.6% beat cons +2.8%. UBS calls it not good enough. Waters volume/mix -1.6% vs +0.8% cons, with adverse weather and Mizone costing about 1ppt of group growth. FY26 guidance of +3% to +5% LFL growth reiterated.

Coca-Cola Q3 beat and guidance raise gives read-across: KO EMEA unit case volumes +5% vs cons +2.9% is positive for Coca-Cola HBC (UBSe Q3 organic sales +8.5% vs cons +8%) on Nigeria and South Africa. For CCEP (UBSe +5.4% vs cons +4.9%), KO called out share loss in France and Great Britain.

Reckitt Q3 missed Street expectations again and the company failed to flag temporary headwinds, as in Q1. UBS argues the setback is one-off, raises FY26 adj EPS 3% to 352p (cons 336p), cuts 2027 EPS 2.5% to 370p (cons 359p) and lifts the target 1% to 7,660p. Rating Buy.
Beiersdorf Q3 gave limited reassurance on NIVEA. Persistently weak sell-out data keeps UBS cautious on market share and the turnaround plan. Rating Neutral, target raised 2.5% to €82.

US tobacco Nielsen to 17 Oct: cigarette volumes -5.7% (prior 4 weeks -6.5%), price/mix +3.2%. Nicotine pouch volumes +10.7% with BAT capturing more than 100% of category volume growth after raising price 18% since December, leaving its price per can in line with ZYN. ZYN original moving from 15 to 20 pouches per can implies a c.25% cut in price per pouch.

Coca-Cola: organic sales growth +7% (+259bps vs Street), FY26 organic sales outlook and adjusted EPS guidance raised, yet shares fell with Staples (XLP -1%) on elevated valuation and doubts about 2027. UBS keeps Buy and expects continued outperformance.

e.l.f. Beauty reports 2Q27 on 11/4 after the close. Shares have outperformed XLP by about 15% since 1Q. UBS sees upside to Street FY27 and FY28 estimates but considers it priced in and would wait for a better entry point. Rating Neutral.

Simply Good Foods guided FY27 sales to -10% to -7%. Adjusted EBITDA came in well below Street on higher brand reinvestment. Shares closed -3.7% vs XLP -0.9%. UBS stays Neutral and sees the outlook as realistic but not de-risked because it is second-half weighted.

Dollar General faces an FTC and multi-state complaint over consumer-protection and weights-and-measures laws. No settlement has been proposed. UBS sees a low probability of changing long-run earnings power. Rating Buy.

Ralph Lauren 2Q27 preview: UBS forecasts a 17c EPS beat and sees a balanced skew because the market already expects a beat-and-raise. Options imply +/-7.3% vs a 6.4% historical average move. UBS raised its target $1 to $521 and keeps Buy.

Under Armour 2Q27 preview: UBS expects a broadly in-line print and reiteration of FY27 EPS guidance of $0.08-$0.12. US website visits down 13% y/y and China online GMV growth slowing to high single digits from 30%. Target cut 11% to $8, Buy retained. Options imply +/-9.5% vs a 10.7% historical average.

Canada Goose 2Q preview: UBS forecasts EPS of -$0.26 vs consensus -$0.23 with FY27 guidance maintained. A 50% tariff on Canadian apparel and weak luxury trends are downside risks. Options imply +/-8.8% vs an 11.3% historical average move. Rating Neutral.
Aritzia investor day: management targets roughly doubling revenue to C$9.5-10.5B by FY32 with adjusted EBITDA margin up about 100bps to 21%. UBS sees a 27% five-year EPS CAGR. Buy reiterated.

Pop Mart Q3 revenue down 45-50% y/y with overseas down 65-75%. Sales were in line, gross margin guidance for 2H was softer than UBS expected, and management expects sequential overseas improvement in Q4. Rating Buy.
Shanghai Bairun Q3 revenue Rmb846mn (+8.3% y/y) and net profit Rmb183mn (+14.0% y/y), in line, driven by whiskey. Buy, target Rmb20.61.

Previews: UBS is ahead of consensus on Campari, CCEP, CCH, Diageo, Magnum Ice Cream, Intercos, Henkel, Richemont and Japan Tobacco. It is below consensus on BIC, Ebro Foods, Haleon, ABI (but in line with the buy side), Ferrari and Hugo Boss. Orkla is a Sell on building margin pressure. Altria is in line, with a pricing step-up that could lift the low end of FY26 guidance.

Markets: KOSPI about +7% after a SK Hynix Q3 print and roughly 100tn won capital return (shares +10%, Samsung +8%), SOX and memory +3-3.5%, TAIEX +2% on OpenAI and Oracle partnerships with Google, and a report that TSMC is raising advanced packaging prices 20%. Crude +1.5-2% with WTI $101.5 and Brent $115.8.

UBS FOMC base case: hold with a 10-2 vote and a hawkish Warsh message of more work to do on inflation, then 25bp hikes in December and January. Markets price about a 10% chance of an October hike, 92% for a December hike and 33bps cumulative by January.

UK Autumn Budget expected to be cautious. Fiscal headroom may have fallen from £23.6bn in March to around £10bn. UBS sees support for gilts, resilient GBP and selective equity opportunities in housebuilders, property, lower-value consumer names and public-investment beneficiaries. A UK bank levy rise is socialised in the press (verbal consensus toward 8% from 3%), while UBS models 3% to 6%, cutting NWG/LLOY numbers 3-4% and BARC/HSBC 1-2%.

European flows Tuesday were 54/46 better to buy with participation about 30% above the YTD run rate. Technology was busiest at 16% of turnover, Industrials were better bid, and Food & Bev, Telecoms, Utilities and Insurance saw supply.

Nielsen: 6 of 13 companies improved. CPB, CAG, UTZ, HSY, KHC down low single digits and SMPL down mid-teens.

earnings_insights: Heineken Q3 (reported 10/28): organic volume +3.9% vs company-compiled consensus +1.8% (UBSe +2.1%), organic revenue +4.6% vs cons +3.5% (UBSe +3.4%). Guidance for FY26 operating profit growth of 2-6% unchanged (cons +5.0%, UBSe +5.3%). 2026E adjusted diluted EPS estimates: cons €5.24, UBSe €5.30. Valuation 14.7x P/E'26.
Heineken new translational FX guidance based on 27 October spot: +€410m net revenue, +€40m consolidated operating profit and +€30m net profit for FY26.

Remy Cointreau Q2 FY27 (reported 10/28): organic sales +4.2% vs cons +3.6% (UBSe +6.5%). Partner Brands -76.7% vs cons -36.0% on the end of Benelux distribution. Leverage target below 3.5x at March 31, 2027 (cons 2.93x, UBSe 2.02x). Valuation 29.3x P/E'26.

Unilever Q3 (reported 10/28): USG +5.2% vs company cons +4.8% (UBSe +5.0%), price +2.3% in line. Beauty & Wellbeing +5.7%, Personal Care +6.3%, Home Care +9.1%, Foods +0.1% vs cons +1.3%. FY26 margin outlook is a modest improvement on 20.0% in FY25 (cons 20.1%). Valuation 17.9x P/E'26.

Danone Q3 (reported 10/28): LFL +4.0% vs cons +3.7% (UBSe +3.8%), pricing +3.6% vs cons +2.8%, volume/mix +0.4% vs cons +0.9%. EDP +3.6%, Specialized Nutrition +4.7%, Waters +3.6% vs cons +4.1%. EMEA +3.9% vs cons +3.0%, Americas +4.4% in line, APAC +3.6% vs cons +3.7%. FY26 LFL guidance +3% to +5% (cons +3.7%). Valuation 15.8x P/E'26.

Reckitt Q3 review (reported): UBS forecasts FY26 core LFL sales growth of 3.7% against guidance of 3.5-4.5%, adjusted operating margin 25.6% (was 25.5%), adjusted EPS 352p (consensus estimate 336p) and 2027 EPS 370p (consensus estimate 359p).
Coca-Cola Q3 (reported): organic sales +7%, +259bps ahead of Street, with better margins driving an EPS beat. FY26 organic sales outlook raised above prior range and adjusted EPS guidance increased.
Simply Good Foods 4QFY26 (reported): EPS beat on top line and margins. FY27 sales guide -10% to -7%, adjusted EBITDA well below Street on brand reinvestment.
Pop Mart Q3 2026 (reported): revenue down 45-50% y/y (domestic -25-30%, APAC -65-70%, Americas -70-75%, Europe and others -50-55%) vs UBS preview estimate of -45%.
Shanghai Bairun 9M26 (reported): revenue Rmb2,503mn and net profit Rmb661mn. Q3 operating margin 27.9% (+1.0pp y/y), net margin 21.6%.

Upcoming (estimates): Ralph Lauren 2Q27 UBS EPS beat forecast of 17c with Street Q3 EPS view $6.86 and FY27 implied EPS outlook of $18.24-$18.96. Under Armour FY27 EPS outlook $0.08-$0.12. Canada Goose Q2 EPS UBSe -$0.26 vs consensus -$0.23. e.l.f. reports 2Q27 on 11/4 after the close.
Japan Tobacco 3Q26E EPS is +2.6% ahead of consensus (UBS estimate), reporting Thursday 10/29. Altria Q3 (10/29) UBS in line with consensus. Haleon and ABI report 10/29.

macro_indicators.reading: UBS base case: hold, likely 10-2 vote, hawkish message from Chair Warsh
macro_indicators.interpretation: Hold reflects proximity of the midterms and sticky inflation around 3% rather than overheating, which reduces urgency to hike immediately.

macro_indicators.reading: 25bp hikes expected in December and January (UBS)
macro_indicators.interpretation: Markets broadly align, pricing about 10% for an October hike, 92% for a December 25bp hike and 33bps cumulative by January.

macro_indicators.reading: around £10bn vs £23.6bn in March, with a rebuilt buffer of roughly £15bn expected
macro_indicators.interpretation: Maintaining fiscal rules should support gilts and GBP resilience into 2027.

macro_indicators.reading: verbal consensus toward 8% from 3%, UBS models 6%
macro_indicators.interpretation: Implied 3-4% cut to NWG and LLOY estimates and 1-2% for BARC and HSBC under UBS's 6% case.

macro_indicators.reading: -5.7% in the 2 weeks to 17 Oct, price/mix +3.2%
macro_indicators.interpretation: Slight improvement from -6.5% over the prior 4 weeks, with industry quarterly pricing put through this month.

trade_ideas.description: Selective UK equity exposure to housebuilders, property, lower-value consumer names and public-investment beneficiaries around the Autumn Budget, rather than a broad UK equity rerating
trade_ideas.rationale: UBS Economics expects a cautious Budget that keeps the fiscal rules, supporting gilts and select domestic sectors.
trade_ideas.risk: A larger-than-modelled bank levy (8% vs UBS's 6%) would cut UK bank estimates further.

risk_factors: Reckitt guidance leaves little room for error after repeated misses against Street expectations and unflagged headwinds.
Staples valuation and 2027 durability: tougher unit case compares, currency and structural headwinds and greater inflation (Coca-Cola).
North America softness at Unilever (-0.7%) and uncertain timing of recovery in Wellbeing and US Foods.
Danone's volume miss with Waters hit by adverse weather and Mizone (about 1ppt drag).
US destocking after distribution changes at Remy Cointreau (Americas and Liqueurs & Spirits).
Pop Mart softer 2H gross margin guidance and a 45-50% y/y revenue decline.
Dollar General FTC and state complaint with uncertain outcome, timing and scope of remedies.
Escalation risk in the Gulf after the US midterms, with crude at WTI $101.5 and Brent $115.8.
Possible UK bank windfall levy increase.
Canada Goose exposure to a 50% tariff on Canadian apparel and weak luxury trends.
Hawkish Fed risk: UBS expects hikes in December and January against sticky inflation near 3%.
vol_and_positioning: Ralph Lauren options imply +/-7.3% over the earnings event vs a 6.4% historical average move. UBS agrees with the options market.
Under Armour options price +/-9.5% vs a 10.7% historical average move. UBS expects less vol than +/-9.5%.
Canada Goose options price +/-8.8% vs an 11.3% historical average move. UBS also expects below-average vol.

European flows Tuesday finished 54/46 better to buy with participation about 30% above the HT YTD run rate. Technology 16% of turnover, balanced with two-way flow in semis. Industrials 14%, better bid across electricals, A&D and maintenance. Banks 14%, with selective UK positioning ahead of the budget.
Market pricing for the FOMC is about a 10% chance of an October hike, 92% for a 25bp December hike and 33bps cumulative by January.
Yesterday's staples tape: XLP -1% on KO day. Best/worst EMEA moves included Beiersdorf -3.29% and Coca-Cola HBC +1.75%. US Hain -3.18% and Hershey -2.21%.
geopolitical: WSJ reported that the US told several Gulf states to prepare for a short, intense military campaign after the midterms, putting escalation risk back on a dated horizon.
UK Autumn Budget today at 13:30 UKT, with a possible windfall tax or levy increase on banks.
A 50% US tariff on Canadian apparel is cited as a downside risk to Canada Goose guidance.
Remy Cointreau tariff impact on operating profit reduced to c.€5m from c.€20m, with nil US impact (previously c.€15m) and c.€5m in China.

tension_points.bull_case: KO delivered organic sales +7%, raised FY26 organic sales and EPS guidance, and UBS sees top and bottom line visibility and a durable long-term organic sales algorithm that warrants a premium.
tension_points.bear_case: Shares fell on staples weakness (XLP -1%), elevated valuation, and doubts that 2026 strength extends. 2027 faces tougher unit case compares, currency and structural headwinds and greater inflation.

tension_points.bull_case: Core-brand momentum, the haircare rollout, fall innovation and rhode's European expansion support Street upside for FY27 and FY28.
tension_points.bear_case: Shares trade at a premium to absolute and relative historical averages and have outperformed XLP by about 15% since 1Q, so upside is largely priced in.
tension_points.what_invalidates: UBS would wait for an attractive entry point and further evidence of upside to its estimates before stepping in.

tension_points.bull_case: UBS checks show solid Q2 fundamentals, a forecast 17c EPS beat and a FY27 guidance raise, and shareholders own RL for long-term potential.
tension_points.bear_case: The market already expects a beat-and-raise, so the print may send Street numbers higher without moving the stock.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Q3 implied EPS guidance failing to bracket the Street's $6.86 view, or a Q2 EPS beat below roughly 15-25c.
